accepted.x: Hiuen Tsang was a Chinese Buddhist monk popularly called the ‘Prince of Pilgrims’; some accounts also refer to him as the ‘King of Travelers’.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive title as a direct name-recall clue.

accepted.s: The travel account of Hiuen Tsang is known as
accepted.x: Hiuen Tsang’s work is Si-Yu-Ki, meaning ‘Records of the Western World’.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the traveller’s account and other historical works.
accepted.sec: Hiuen Tsang - reign, route, places, Si-Yu-Ki, observations

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes Si-Yu-Ki attributed to Hiuen Tsang?
o: A Buddhist philosophical treatise composed at Ajanta
A biography of Harshavardhana written by Bana
A short account restricted to the Gupta court
The longest and most detailed account of Central and South Asia
accepted.x: Si-Yu-Ki is regarded as the longest and most detailed account of Central and South Asia among the works associated with Hiuen Tsang.
accepted.tq: Choose the precise descriptive statement rather than a work-person trap.
accepted.sec: Hiuen Tsang - reign, route, places, Si-Yu-Ki, observations

accepted.s:
Which of the following places were visited by Hiuen Tsang as important Buddhist sites?
1. Lumbini
2. Kapilavastu
3. Bodh Gaya
4. Sarnath
5. Kushinara
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Hiuen Tsang visited all five listed Buddhist sites: Lumbini, Kapilavastu, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath and Kushinara.
accepted.tq: Test completeness of a named list by checking every item.
accepted.sec: Hiuen Tsang - reign, route, places, Si-Yu-Ki, observations

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding places described by Hiuen Tsang:
1. Bhinmal was described as a Gurjara capital.
2. The Sun temple of Multan was mentioned in his account.
3. Pataliputra had retained its position as the premier city of northern India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Bhinmal was described as a Gurjara capital and the Sun temple of Multan was mentioned. Hiuen Tsang observed that Kannauj, not Pataliputra, had become the premier city.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed comparison in statement 3.
accepted.sec: Hiuen Tsang - reign, route, places, Si-Yu-Ki, observations

accepted.s: According to Hiuen Tsang’s observations, which one of the following combinations is correct?
o: No taxation and unrestricted local autonomy
Rigid taxation and complete absence of officials
Light taxation and freedom from oppression by officials
accepted.x: Hiuen Tsang described taxation as not heavy and stated that subjects were free from oppression by officials.
accepted.tq: Match the social observation with its exact administrative description.
accepted.sec: Hiuen Tsang - reign, route, places, Si-Yu-Ki, observations

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding law and order during Harsha’s period, as observed by Hiuen Tsang, is correct?
o: The kingdom was poorly governed and experienced continuous revolts.
The kingdom was well governed and had no revolts, although Hiuen Tsang was robbed twice.
Robbery was unknown because roads were guarded by the army.
Hiuen Tsang was robbed only after leaving Harsha’s kingdom.
accepted.x: Hiuen Tsang described the kingdom as well governed and free from revolts, but recorded that he himself was robbed twice.
accepted.tq: Reconcile two apparently contrasting details instead of choosing an extreme statement.
accepted.sec: Hiuen Tsang - reign, route, places, Si-Yu-Ki, observations

accepted.s: Hiuen Tsang’s account indicates that the economy of the period was marked by
o: rapid expansion of overseas trade and urbanisation
complete dependence on imported food grains
decline of trade and the rise of a self-sufficient agrarian economy
accepted.x: He noticed signs of declining trade and the growth of a self-sufficient, agrarian economy.
accepted.tq: Identify the paired trend rather than reversing one element of the comparison.
accepted.sec: Hiuen Tsang - reign, route, places, Si-Yu-Ki, observations

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT an observation attributed to Hiuen Tsang?
o: Brahmanism was rising while Buddhism was declining.
The position of women had declined, though women were not treated as inferior.
The caste system was rigid and untouchables were mentioned.
Jainism was specifically described as the principal rising religion.
accepted.x: Hiuen Tsang mentioned rigid caste distinctions, untouchables, the declining position of women and the rise of Brahmanism. He did not mention Jainism in this observation.
accepted.tq: Find the single statement outside the recorded set of observations.
accepted.sec: Hiuen Tsang - reign, route, places, Si-Yu-Ki, observations

accepted.s:
Hiuen Tsang praised which of the following rulers?
1. Harshavardhana
2. Pulakesin II
3. Narasimhavarman
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Hiuen Tsang praised Harsha, Pulakesin II of the Chalukyas and Narasimhavarman of the Pallavas.

accepted.s: Who founded the Vakataka dynasty?
accepted.x: Vindhyashakti is regarded as the founder of the Vakataka dynasty.
accepted.tq: Use the founder–dynasty association directly; do not confuse founder with a later great ruler.
accepted.sec: Vakatakas - founder, branches, Prabhavatigupta, Pravarasena, Ajanta

accepted.s:
With reference to Pravarasena I, consider the following statements:
1. He was the son of Vindhyashakti.
2. He was the only Vakataka ruler to assume the title Samrat.
3. He performed Vajapeya and Ashvamedha sacrifices.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Pravarasena I was Vindhyashakti’s son, the only Vakataka ruler to take the title Samrat, and performed Vajapeya and Ashvamedha sacrifices.
accepted.tq: Combine lineage, title and ritual facts in one coded question.
accepted.sec: Vakatakas - founder, branches, Prabhavatigupta, Pravarasena, Ajanta

accepted.s: The two principal branches of the Vakataka dynasty were associated with which pair of centres?
accepted.x: The main branch was associated with Nandivardhana and Pravarapura, while the Vatsagulma branch was associated with Basim.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure branch–centre pair and eliminate crossed locations.
accepted.sec: Vakatakas - founder, branches, Prabhavatigupta, Pravarasena, Ajanta

accepted.s: Prabhavatigupta was the daughter of Chandragupta II and was married to
accepted.x: Prabhavatigupta, daughter of Chandragupta II, married the Vakataka ruler Rudrasena II.
accepted.tq: Discriminate a marriage link from nearby Vakataka ruler relationships.
accepted.sec: Vakatakas - founder, branches, Prabhavatigupta, Pravarasena, Ajanta

accepted.s: What was the political significance of Prabhavatigupta’s regency after the death of Rudrasena II?
o: It ended Gupta influence in western India.
It established direct Harshavardhana rule over the Deccan.
It brought indirect Gupta control over the Deccan.
It transferred Vakataka power to the Pallavas.
accepted.x: Prabhavatigupta’s regency enabled the Guptas to exercise indirect control over the Deccan through the Vakataka kingdom.
accepted.tq: Infer the political consequence from the marriage and regency relationship.
accepted.sec: Vakatakas - founder, branches, Prabhavatigupta, Pravarasena, Ajanta

accepted.s: Who wrote the Prakrit work Setubandha?
accepted.x: Pravarasena II wrote the Prakrit work Setubandha.
accepted.tq: Apply the author–work pairing without confusing Pravarasena I and II.
accepted.sec: Vakatakas - founder, branches, Prabhavatigupta, Pravarasena, Ajanta

accepted.s: Harishena of the Vatsagulma branch is associated with the patronage of which Ajanta caves through his minister Varahadeva?
accepted.x: Harishena patronised Ajanta Caves 16 and 17 through his minister Varahadeva.
accepted.tq: Test the exact cave-number pair rather than the general Ajanta association.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship of the listed rulers or kingdoms with Harsha?
o: Grahavarman of Kannauj was Harsha’s ally and survived the Malwa attack.
Sasanka of Gauda was Harsha’s enemy and killed Rajyavardhana.
Dhruvasena II of Valabhi was Harsha’s principal enemy.
Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa killed Rajyavardhana and opposed Harsha.
accepted.x: Sasanka of Gauda was Harsha’s enemy and was responsible for the killing of Rajyavardhana. Grahavarman was Harsha’s brother-in-law, Bhaskaravarman was his ally and Dhruvasena II was his vassal and son-in-law.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–relationship trap by checking who was ally, enemy, vassal or victim.

accepted.s: The Maukharis had their capital at
accepted.x: Kannauj was the capital of the Maukharis. Grahavarman, a Maukhari ruler, was the husband of Rajyashri.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a kingdom’s capital from the capitals of neighbouring post-Gupta powers.

accepted.s: Who is identified in the stated chronological tradition as the founder of the Vardhana or Pushyabhuti line in the late fifth or early sixth century?
accepted.x: Naravardhana is identified as the founder of the Vardhana line in the late fifth or early sixth century; Prabhakaravardhana was its first great ruler.
accepted.tq: Separate the dynastic founder from the first prominent ruler and later members.

A. Adityavardhana
B. Prabhakaravardhana

D. Harshavardhana

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Vardhana lineage is correct?
1. Prabhakaravardhana was the father of Rajyavardhana and Harsha.
2. Yashomati, the queen of Prabhakaravardhana, became sati in 605 CE.
3. Rajyavardhana was killed by Sasanka.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: Prabhakaravardhana was their father, Yashomati became sati in 605 CE, and Rajyavardhana was killed by Sasanka.
accepted.tq: Combine family relationship, date and political event in a single statement set.
accepted.sec: Post-Gupta kingdoms and Vardhana lineage

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Kannauj assembly from the Prayag assembly?
o: Kannauj was held every five years for charity, whereas Prayag honoured Hiuen Tsang.
Prayag was a one-time debate attended only by Buddhist scholars.
Kannauj honoured Hiuen Tsang and promoted Mahayana, whereas Prayag was associated with charity.
Both assemblies were held at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna.
accepted.x: The Kannauj assembly honoured Hiuen Tsang and propagated Mahayana, while the Prayag assembly was primarily a charitable gathering held periodically.
accepted.tq: Split the alternatives by purpose and frequency before considering location.
accepted.sec: Kannauj assembly and Prayag assembly

accepted.s: The Kannauj assembly convened by Harshavardhana was held in
accepted.x: The Kannauj assembly is dated to 643 CE.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the assembly year from Hiuen Tsang’s court date and Harsha’s other chronological markers.
accepted.sec: Kannauj assembly and Prayag assembly

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kannauj assembly:
1. It was held to honour Hiuen Tsang and propagate Mahayana doctrine.
2. It lasted for 23 days according to the stated APP account.
3. It ended without any disturbance or attempt on Harsha’s life.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The assembly honoured Hiuen Tsang, propagated Mahayana and lasted 23 days in the stated account. It was followed by violence, arson and an attempt on Harsha’s life, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Identify the negative event that reverses an otherwise correct account of the assembly.
accepted.sec: Kannauj assembly and Prayag assembly

accepted.s: Which one of the following events is associated with the conclusion of the Kannauj assembly?
o: An arson incident and an attempt on Harsha’s life occurred.
Hiuen Tsang returned to Central Asia through Afghanistan.
The Vakataka branch at Vatsagulma was established.
Harsha gave away his entire treasury at the Ganga-Yamuna confluence.
accepted.x: The Kannauj assembly was followed by violence, including arson and an attempt to assassinate Harsha.
accepted.tq: Match the assembly with its distinctive concluding incident.
accepted.sec: Kannauj assembly and Prayag assembly

accepted.s: The Prayag assembly, also known as the Moksha Parishad, was held at
o: The confluence of the Narmada and Tapti
Kannauj on the banks of the Ganga
The confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna
accepted.x: The Prayag assembly was held at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna at Prayag, also known as Allahabad.
accepted.tq: Use the location-specific geographical clue to distinguish the two assemblies.
accepted.sec: Kannauj assembly and Prayag assembly

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the principal purpose of the Prayag assembly?
accepted.x: The Prayag assembly was associated with charity or dana and was held every five years.
accepted.tq: Separate religious propagation at Kannauj from charitable giving at Prayag.
accepted.sec: Kannauj assembly and Prayag assembly

accepted.s:
With reference to the Prayag assembly, consider the following statements:
1. It was held every five years.
2. Harsha gave away his treasury and retained only his personal clothes.
3. Hiuen Tsang attended the sixth such assembly.
4. It represented only Mahayana Buddhists.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Prayag assembly was held every five years, Harsha distributed his treasury while retaining only his clothes, and Hiuen Tsang attended the sixth assembly. Representatives of all religions attended, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the exclusivist word ‘only’ when the assembly included representatives of all religions.
accepted.sec: Kannauj assembly and Prayag assembly

accepted.s: The worship of the Buddha, the Sun and Shiva on successive days at the Prayag assembly indicates Harsha’s
o: strict adherence to one religious sect
accepted.x: The successive worship of the Buddha, the Sun and Shiva is presented as evidence of Harsha’s eclecticism.
accepted.tq: Infer the ruler’s religious outlook from the sequence of practices.
accepted.sec: Kannauj assembly and Prayag assembly
